messages:
Priya: heads-up: customer Nyx requested we validate two merge strategies for their adapter: stitch (full-merge) vs graft (LoRA overlay). Problem observed in staging: code-block formatting and small-amount cents disappear in the grafted int4 probe. Need a quick compare pack.

Connor: I'll build a bifurcated eval: `nyx_stitch_vs_graft` with 800 prompts split equally. Tests: invoice amounts, short JS code blocks, date normalization, and OCR-style inputs. Will annotate expected canonical outputs.

Marta: Note: last time the stitch preserved punctuation better but increased latency. Graft is cheaper but lost "," tokens. Let's also test an experimental int3-lite quant profile (`bnb3-lite`) on a tiny shadow to see extremes.

Priya: Good call. Run matrix: float32 baseline, int8, bnb4-hybrid, bnb4, bnb3-lite. Also include `--kv-policy preserve-prefix` vs `--kv-policy compact` to see KV effects. Use dedicated-nyx-02 for fairness.

eval-bot: queued run at 1700000200, run_id=nyx-1700000123-compare-1, matrix jobs scheduled. Will post topline metrics as jobs complete.

Noah: tiny reminder: if code blocks are being reformatted, check tokenizer pretokenize flags and streaming chunk sizes; those affect backslash/newline handling in generation.

eval-bot: preliminary: float32=98/100; int8=95/100; bnb4-hybrid=92/100; bnb4=75/100; bnb3-lite=60/100. Major diffs: grafted bnb4 loses trailing ".00" in 14% of currency prompts, bnb3-lite drops punctuation in code fences (~25% of samples).

Marta: patch idea: for graft runs try `--lora-scale 0.6` and a short targeted re-bias of 800 steps focusing on token ids [",", ".", "0"] and code fence tokens (```). That might recover punctuation without full retrain.

Connor: spinning graft + rebias + kv-preserve run now: `rwi run --model nyx-finetune-v3 --merge graft --lora-scale 0.6 --retrain-steps 800 --quant bnb4-hybrid --kv-policy preserve-prefix --eval nyx_stitch_vs_graft --workers 10`

eval-bot: graft+rebias run queued at 1700000400, run_id=nyx-1700000123-2. Streaming diffs available.

eval-bot: graft+rebias summary: pass=90/100. Currency cents failures down from 14 -> 3; code fence formatting failures down from 12 -> 2. Latency: +4% vs graft baseline, +9% vs stitch.

Priya: promising. Stitch run for baseline of full-merge: `rwi run --model nyx-finetune-v3 --merge stitch --quant bnb4-hybrid --eval nyx_stitch_vs_graft --workers 8`

eval-bot: stitch run complete: pass=93/100. Stitch preserved punctuation best but cost of compute higher. For tight SLAs, stitch might be borderline.

Marta: recommendation: keep prod default on int8; for Dedicated-Nyx allow two rollout options: 1) stitch+b4-hybrid for high-fidelity endpoints, 2) graft+rebias+b4-hybrid for cost-sensitive endpoints, with nightly shadow of bnb3-lite only for benchmark data collection.

Connor: logging artifacts: uploaded token-prob traces, per-example diffs, and a mini dashboard comparing parse success rates and latency. Links: https://artifacts.internal/nyx/1700000123/compare.

Noah: I'll open INFR-5502 to verify quant kernels and ensure same kernel versions between dedicated and hosted. Also check streaming chunking knobs.

Priya: action list: Connor keep graft+rebias job as repeatable job, Marta document stitch SLA tradeoffs in the rollout playbook, Noah confirm kernel parity. We'll shadow graft+rebias on a small customer cohort for 48h before any wider promotion. Thanks. :white_check_mark:
